brand: charcoal and sage; no purple, neon, emoji or gold
question: Does certify/20l (an L*-style learner that chooses its own actions to fill an observation table and to execute counterexample words, and that issues ID / IDF only through certify/16e's UNSAT rival proofs at the declared N) decide more fresh noise-free 20-state worlds than certify/16e at the same conflict budget (B20 2000000, C20 50000), while staying sound, deterministic under a conflict-only stop, faithful, and compatible with certify/16e at bound 16?

hypotheses.H1: certify/20l issues no WRONG certificate on 6 fresh 20-state worlds over two passes (12 records) or on 6 clean 16-state controls
hypotheses.H2: with a conflict-only stop on a 4-worker pool, the two certify/20l passes give byte-identical canonical records on 6/6 cases with identical conflict counts and 0 hard kills
hypotheses.H3: every certify/20l record is reproduced exactly by api_checks driving certify/20l observation by observation (run once)
hypotheses.H4: at bound 16 certify/20l gives the same label as certify/16e on 6/6 fresh clean 16-state controls and, under compat_rule_056, the same machine. Inferred risk declared pre-data: certify/20l chooses different actions than certify/16e, so the traces and stop steps will differ (as in 055)
hypotheses.H5: certify/20l ID+IDF >= 2/6 on scale20t and strictly more than certify/16e at bound 20 on the same seeds. Inferred risk declared pre-data: the final UNSAT rival proof at N = 20 may itself exceed 2M conflicts even when the hypothesis is right; in that case the learner only moves the hardness from the least-machine search to the proof

design.api: one new module brute/api/certify20l.py (certify/20l), same observe / propose / result interface, labels and K as certify/16e. certify/16n, certify/16e, certify/16s, certify/20t and certify/20c and every earlier module are imported only, never edited. Host-agnostic: no I/O, threads, subprocess or os.
design.learner: no-reset L* (Rivest-Schapire style, because the world has no reset and a run is one walk): a homing word h, fixed before data as the shortest word over the 3 actions that the learner's table distinguishes after each step, starts each table round; rows are access words from the current homed state, columns are distinguishing suffixes; the learner proposes the next word needed to fill a missing table cell. When the table is closed and consistent it gives a hypothesis H with at most N states; if it has more than N rows the case stops AMB with the table published (no claim).
design.equivalence: no oracle: the equivalence check is certify/16e's rival query at size N on the trace so far (another machine with <= N states consistent with the trace that differs from H on the future, or on the start). SAT -> the rival's shortest distinguishing word from the current state is the counterexample; the learner proposes it next and adds its suffixes as columns (Rivest-Schapire split). UNSAT on 'future' -> IDF; UNSAT on 'future' and 'start' -> ID, labels exactly as certify/16e.
design.solver: CaDiCaL through the same incremental pool as certify/16e, chunks of C20 = 50000 conflicts, one case budget B20 = 2000000 summed over every SAT call (B 3000000 at bound 16 for compat); budget spent -> IDU; no least-machine SAT search (H comes from the table, the size lower bound is the number of table rows)
design.determinism: homing word, column order, cell-fill order (shortest-lex) and counterexample choice (shortest, then lex) are fixed before data; no wall time, randomness or solver statistics affect any choice
design.soundness: Exact argument, checked by tests and GS_ref: every ID / IDF is issued only on an UNSAT rival proof over all machines with <= N states consistent with the full trace, the same claim as certify/16e; the table only chooses actions and the candidate H. A wrong H can cost budget, never a WRONG label
design.stop: conflict-only stop for all arms; 900 s per-case hard kill as a safety net (any kill fails GDET56)

certification_rule: certify/20l becomes certified for declared N <= 20 on noise-free traces iff every gated criterion passes, GS20L_gain56 included. If every gate except GS20L_gain56 passes, certify/20l is published as sound but not certified. If any other gate fails as well, certify/20l has no certification status.
